extracted.intended_audience: regulated entities, state and local environmental/air-quality agencies, environmental lawyers and consultants, stakeholders and public commenters
extracted.subtask_description: A machine-readable listing of EPA proposed-rule Federal Register notices summarizing proposed regulatory actions, associated legal standards, procedural steps (e.g., comment periods, hearings), and conditional approval/withdrawal rationales for state and federal programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: SIP revision noninterference requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: "will not interfere with any applicable requirement concerning attainment and reasonable further progress or any other applicable requirement of the Clean Air Act (CAA or Act)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA proposes to approve State Implementation Plan (SIP) revisions only if the revision will not interfere with attainment, reasonable further progress (RFP), or other CAA requirements; this is the basic legal gate for SIP approval and is cited as the basis for approving removal/changes to state programs (e.g., vehicle I/M programs).

rubrics_metrics.name: SIP/attainment plan required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: An attainment plan must include "the State's attainment demonstration and other elements required under Clean Air Act (CAA). In addition to an attainment demonstration, the plan addresses emission limitations necessary to provide for attainment, base-year and projection-year emission inventories, reasonably available control measures and reasonably available control technology (RACM/RACT), nonattainment new source review (NNSR), the requirements for meeting reasonable further progress (RFP) toward attainment of the NAAQS, and contingency measures."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating an attainment plan, EPA looks for each of these enumerated elements; absence or inadequacy of any element can be a basis for disapproval or conditional approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional approval of local rules under the CAA
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA can "conditionally approve a local rule to regulate these emission sources under the Clean Air Act (CAA or 'Act')."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditional approval may be used where a state or local rule largely meets CAA requirements but depends on corrective actions or further commitments; EPA will solicit comments and follow with a final action.

rubrics_metrics.name: RACT/RACT compliance for state rules
rubrics_metrics.description: State rules implementing statewide reasonably available control technology (RACT) requirements must limit emissions (e.g., NOX) from covered sources to meet CAA obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA reviews state regulations for adequacy of RACT implementation; SIP approval is proposed where the regulations satisfy statewide RACT requirements. Expect EPA to review emission limits, applicability, and enforceability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program approval under RCRA standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A state's Coal Combustion Residuals (CCR) partial permit program must "meet the standard for approval under RCRA."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA preliminarily determines whether a state-submitted program satisfies statutory and regulatory requirements under RCRA; approval enables the state program to operate in lieu of the Federal program except where noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment period and extension practice
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA provides a public comment period on proposed rules and may extend the comment period (examples: 60-day comment period; extensions of 22 days, 30 days, or other periods).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA will extend or reopen comment periods to allow additional review and input (e.g., in response to public requests). Notices will specify the new deadline and often the reason for extension (administrative correction, stakeholder request, complexity of proposal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopening comment period on request
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA can reopen the comment period "in response to a request in a public comment" and set a new comment deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A public commenter or stakeholder may request additional time; EPA may decide to reopen the comment period if it considers the request appropriate to allow fuller participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: SNUR notification and waiting period (TSCA)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Significant New Use Rules (SNURs) under TSCA, the SNURs "require persons to notify EPA at least 90 days before commencing the manufacture (defined by statute to include import) or processing of any of these chemical substances for an activity that is designated as a significant new use in the SNUR."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 90-day notification initiates EPA's evaluation; manufacture or processing for the significant new use may not commence until EPA completes its review, makes an appropriate determination, and takes required actions. This is a statutory procedural bar on starting the activity until EPA acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noninterference with NAAQS attainment/maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule revisions must "not interfere with the State's ability to attain or maintain the National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA evaluates whether state rule changes would adversely affect attainment/maintenance of NAAQS; if they would, EPA will not approve the revision. EPA checks modeled/observed impacts and related control measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory revisions consistency and non-duplication
rubrics_metrics.description: Revisions may be approved when they revise "unnecessarily restrictive or duplicative language," add appropriate definitions and incorporations by reference, and align with similar rules in other areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA supports clarifying edits, threshold changes, and streamlining (e.g., eliminating redundant permitting requirements) provided they do not reduce required protections or enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: State plan requirements for existing sources (111(d)/EG)
rubrics_metrics.description: A State Plan implementing Emissions Guidelines (EG) for existing municipal solid waste (MSW) landfills must establish emission limits, monitoring, operating, recordkeeping, and reporting requirements for affected landfills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA reviews the State Plan for completeness and enforceability of limits and procedural requirements; the Plan must implement and enforce the EG in effect (citation: EG finalized by EPA on August 29, 2016 in this example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology review scope under NESHAP (section 112)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under a technology review pursuant to Clean Air Act section 112, EPA may propose no revisions to current standards, propose standards for unregulated pollutants (resulting in no additional control requirements), or propose alternative approaches for previously unregulated emission points (defer or set new control standards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA's section 112(d)(6) review evaluates whether to regulate additional emission points or pollutants; the Agency may choose to defer regulation or adopt new emission limits and associated technical corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition alignment to reduce burdens
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA may propose changes to regulatory definitions (e.g., "associated equipment") "to align with the CAA that, if finalized, would reduce burdens on industry."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes to definitional language are evaluated for legal alignment and practical burden reduction; EPA may justify such changes as reducing unnecessary regulatory obligations while remaining consistent with statutory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor technical corrections as an administrative criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA may propose "minor technical corrections to the existing regulations."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical corrections fix typographical, citation, or formatting errors and are not intended to change substantive requirements; EPA may include such corrections within a broader proposed action.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERC generation via mobile-source reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: A program can allow fleet owners/operators to generate emission reduction credits (ERCs) by retrofitting or replacing existing fleet vehicles with lower emitting vehicles while meeting CAA requirements; ERCs can be used as offsets under Nonattainment New Source Review (NNSR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA evaluates whether the ERC generation methodology is federally enforceable, verifiable, surplus, quantifiable, and consistent with NNSR offset requirements before approving the SIP revision enabling such a program.

rubrics_metrics.name: CCR regulatory changes and site-specific permitting pathway
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals may establish a new compliance pathway allowing for site-specific considerations for CCR permitting (monitoring points of compliance, cleanup levels for corrective action, closure requirements and timeframes, CCR extraction for beneficial use during post-closure care), revise beneficial-use definitions, define CCR storage piles, and exclude specific beneficial uses from federal CCR regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA will evaluate how site-specific flexibility affects protectiveness, groundwater/runoff risks, and consistency with statutory CCR obligations; changes to beneficial-use criteria will affect which uses are regulated and which are excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of international emission considerations in attainment determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA may determine that an area "would have attained the [NAAQS] by the Moderate area attainment date but for emissions emanating from outside the United States (U.S.)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When international transport significantly impedes attainment, EPA can consider foreign emissions in deciding whether reclassification or additional CAA obligations should apply; this can justify repeal of prior failure-to-attain determinations or reclassification actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attainment date extension criteria based on monitoring data
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA may propose to grant an extension of the attainment date (e.g., a second 1-year extension) and determine attainment based on certified ozone monitoring data covering a specified period (e.g., 2020-2022).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions require demonstration that the area meets statutory criteria (e.g., submission requirements, attainment despite exceptional events, or other legal bases) and EPA's review of certified monitoring data to support the extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Startup, shutdown, and malfunction (SSM) provision adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: SIP revisions to startup and shutdown provisions must avoid deficiencies previously identified by EPA (e.g., disapproved portions) and be amended to address those deficiencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA evaluates SSM provisions for enforceability and whether they create unauthorized exemptions from emission limits; revisions must close gaps that led to earlier disapproval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative corrections and docket accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA issues corrections to procedural items (e.g., incorrect docket number) and may extend comment periods to allow public participation after corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative corrections ensure the record is accurate and that the public has access to the correct docket; EPA may extend deadlines when errors would otherwise impede meaningful comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infrastructure SIP (section 110) adequacy — interstate visibility and prong tests
rubrics_metrics.description: A state's infrastructure submission must "contain adequate provisions prohibiting emissions that will interfere with required visibility protection measures in any other State's SIP" (Prong 4) and otherwise satisfy the structural components required under section 110 of the CAA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA assesses whether the state's SIP contains enforceable measures and regulatory structure (monitoring, enforcement, legal authority) sufficient to prevent interstate transport that would interfere with another state's visibility programs or NAAQS.
